behavioral_notes.observation: Turns a calendar's weekly attendance_ids (resource.calendar.attendance: dayofweek + hour_from/hour_to per morning/lunch/afternoon period) into concrete (begin_dt, end_dt, attendance) tuples for any datetime range, using a dateutil rrule over the requested weekdays. It handles the two-week alternating calendar (week_type via get_week_type = parity of the ordinal-week number), per-resource timezones (it groups resources by tz and localizes the generic UTC interval skeleton once per tz), and flexible / duration-based schedules (fully-flexible resources get the whole range as one dummy attendance; flexible calendars synthesise daily intervals centred on 12:00 until hours_per_week is met). This Intervals math is the substrate every scheduling consumer relies on and is wholly invisible in field/relation metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: resource.calendar._work_intervals_batch (attendances minus leaves = effective working time)
behavioral_notes.observation: Effective work intervals = _attendance_intervals_batch MINUS _leave_intervals_batch (Intervals set difference), keyed per resource id (with the False key = the calendar-generic resource). This single method is THE capacity-calculation join point downstream apps call: get_work_hours_count / get_work_duration_data (hours + days for a period), plan_hours / plan_days (find the datetime N working hours/days away), _get_closest_work_time + resource.resource._adjust_to_calendar (snap a datetime to the nearest working boundary), and _unavailable_intervals (the off-hours gaps, used by enterprise planning/forecast gantt). Grep confirms hr, hr_attendance, hr_calendar, hr_holidays, hr_timesheet, hr_work_entry and mrp all call into these methods. None of this control flow is reverse-engineerable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: resource.calendar.leaves (global vs resource-specific time off) feeding _leave_intervals_batch
behavioral_notes.observation: A leave row with resource_id = False is a GLOBAL company time-off (public holiday / closure) that subtracts from every resource sharing that calendar/company; a leave with resource_id set subtracts only for that one resource. time_type ('leave' vs 'other') controls whether the row counts as absence or as work-equivalent time (e.g. training). _leave_intervals_batch expresses date_from/date_to (stored naive-UTC) in each resource's tz before differencing, and routes flexible-resource leaves through _handle_flexible_leave_interval (expanded to whole days). hr_holidays's approved time off and the work-entry modules write into this exact table, so resource is the shared sink where absences become unavailable capacity.

Every public computation method asserts tzinfo on its datetimes (naive inputs are made explicit as UTC via tools.date_utils.localized), converts to the resource/calendar tz (resource.tz | calendar.tz, default 'UTC') for the interval comparison, and reverts to the caller's tz on the way out (to_timezone). resource.calendar.tz_offset is computed from the tz selection; resource.resource and resource.mixin carry a related tz so an employee / work-center inherits one. The whole module is a timezone-correctness layer so 'working hours' mean the local clock, not server UTC -- a correctness concern code-read makes visible that metadata cannot.

5 JS files, 2 XML templates, 0 OWL components, 2 registry adds ('fields:section_one2many' for the sectioned working-time list editor, 'views:form_description_expander'); bundles ['web.assets_backend', 'web.assets_unit_tests']. The UI is a thin form/list editor for the calendar grid, not an interactive client app -- consistent with resource being backend master-data infrastructure.

classification.rationale: resource is the working-time / capacity-calculation BACKBONE of Odoo, not a primary value-creating activity: it owns the working-schedule master data (resource.calendar + attendance grid + time off) and the interval engine (_work_intervals_batch / _attendance_intervals_batch / plan_hours / get_work_hours_count) that other modules call to know WHEN and HOW MUCH a resource works. It is value-model 'support' and activity_class 'support' under Stabell & Fjeldstad / Porter -- firm infrastructure, exactly analogous to analytic for costs: where analytic is the shared vessel for cost/revenue, resource is the shared vessel for working-time and availability. Grep confirms hr, hr_attendance, hr_calendar, hr_holidays, hr_timesheet, hr_work_entry and mrp all depend on its engine. APQC mapping = 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital, the same category as the hr module, because the dominant use is workforce scheduling and time/absence management (manage employee work schedules and time off via resource.calendar / resource.calendar.leaves) and resource.resource models the workforce/work-center whose capacity HR and operations plan. It is NOT 8.0 Manage Information Technology (this is business scheduling data, not IT infrastructure/services) and NOT merely 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities (too generic -- 13.0 is knowledge/program management, whereas resource's concrete domain is the human-capital working calendar). Its material-resource / work-center reuse (mrp) means it also underpins manufacturing capacity planning, but human-capital working-time is the defining, original purpose, so 7.0 is the primary APQC home.
